sample_unit: patients in prospective crossover trial (12 endoscopists)
models_evaluated: joint-AI model (multimodal EUS images plus clinical information)

links.outcome: Endoscopist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance in randomized crossover trial
links.effect: Novice endoscopist accuracy rose from 0.69 (95% CI, 0.61-0.76) without AI to 0.90 (95% CI, 0.83-0.94) with AI assistance (P < .001).
links.quote: The diagnostic accuracy of novice endoscopists was significantly enhanced with AI assistance (0.69 [95% CI, 0.61-0.76] vs 0.90 [95% CI, 0.83-0.94]; P < .001), and the supplementary interpretability information alleviated the skepticism of the experienced endoscopists.

links.outcome: Model AUC on internal versus external multicenter test datasets
links.effect: AUC was 0.996 (95% CI, 0.993-0.998) internally and 0.955, 0.924, and 0.976 in the 3 external test datasets, showing a modest drop externally.
links.quote: The area under the curve of the joint-AI model ranged from 0.996 (95% CI, 0.993-0.998) in the internal test dataset to 0.955 (95% CI, 0.940-0.968), 0.924 (95% CI, 0.888-0.955), and 0.976 (95% CI, 0.942-0.995) in the 3 external test datasets, respectively.

unlisted_practices: Supplying interpretability information (explanations) alongside AI output to reduce skepticism of experienced clinicians

screen.reason: The study conducts a randomized crossover reader trial comparing endoscopists' diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance and interpretability information.

primary.practice: AI-assisted clinician review with interpretability feedback
